How scalable, governed data and AI platforms are unlocking true enterprise transformation. This discussion brought together David Brown ( ViiV Healthcare ), Mostafa Taha (Merck), gelsomino centanni ( Novartis ) and Alan Kalton , Principal at Axtria - Ingenious Insights . to explore how unified data platforms with governance embedded by design create secure, interoperable, and AI‑ready foundations across both commercial and regulated environments. The panel also emphasised the importance of simplifying AI and analytics at scale 🤖📊 by equipping teams with tested tools, templates, and reliable platforms so successful pilots can quickly evolve into repeatable, enterprise-wide solutions 🚀. #REPharma #DataPlatforms #AIGovernance #EnterpriseTransformation #AnalyticsAtScale #PharmaInnovation

Last week I closed a chapter of my career. Twenty years in pharma, working at large companies and small ones, agencies, and even consulting. I always knew it wasn't forever. I told myself that for a decade: when the time is right, I'm going to do something that's fully mine. That time is now. When J&J laid me off in 2024, I treated it as the push I needed. I got certified as a professional coach and started building what comes next. I've spent twenty years in rooms where the most useful thing I could do was ask why. Why are we solving it this way? Why does this feel stuck? That instinct doesn't go away. It just found a better home. I've launched Inner Spark Coaching to work with driven women navigating that quiet but persistent feeling that something needs to change. The questions are the same ones I asked in high-stakes brand strategy rooms: What are we actually solving for? What's really in the way? Are we even looking at this from the right angle? Turns out they work just as well on a career crossroads as they do on a product launch. True or false: most people aren't stuck because they don't know what to do. They're stuck because they do know, but it's scary. #womeninleadership #lifeafterpharma #Pharmamarketing

Pride Month has always felt personal to me — a time to celebrate progress, but also to recognize that there is still more to do. At ViiV Healthcare , our commitment to the LGBTQ+ community isn’t something we switch on in June. It’s part of how we show up every day — listening to communities, building real partnerships, and acting on what we hear. Because HIV — and the stigma around it — is still a reality for far too many people. I was proud to be in Durham with our ViiV US team and the Durham Bulls Baseball Club to celebrate Pride together - just one of many ways our teams will be showing up with communities across the country for Pride. Moments like this matter. And I don’t take for granted that not everyone, everywhere, has the same opportunity to show up, be visible, and be supported. Thank you to the Durham Bulls for hosting us — and for the chance to throw out the first pitch (definitely a memorable first for me). What I’ve learned over time is that progress starts with listening. Really listening — to lived experiences, to perspectives that challenge us, and to voices that too often go unheard. Pride is a moment to reflect. But more importantly, it’s a moment to recommit. Because this work — driven by people, partnership, and courage — doesn’t stop in June. #WeWontStop #PrideMonth #EndingHIV

We did it — we were the first all-women's crew to row the Channel! Last Friday morning, we set off to conquer the Channel as a crew of nine, including my wonderful crewmates Aigerim Saudabayeva, Claire Edwards , Sian Gill , Wendy Armstrong , Meredith Ellis , Nile Verleur , Kate Taylor and Sally Foster. Our pilot boat skipper predicted it would take 12 hours to row the 35 nautical miles from Ramsgate to Dunkirk, but he hadn't reckoned on a crew of Oriel women rowers. We completed the crossing in 9 hours and 41 minutes! The challenge reinforced for me the grit, strength and camaraderie of Oriel rowing. We were the sixth and final Oriel alumni crew to successfully cross the Channel as part of a campaign to establish an endowment fund for Oriel College, Oxford Boat Club. We rowed for every future Oriel student who will pick up an oar and discover, as we did, the friendships, resilience, and opportunities that rowing can provide. Thank you to everyone who has supported the Oriel crews on this journey. If you haven't yet donated and have a connection to Oriel or Oxford, we'd be hugely grateful for your support. Every contribution will help ensure future generations of Oriel rowers can benefit from the same transformative experience: https://lnkd.in/eqk6QxTZ Please can I also ask you to add a quick comment below?

Not Retiring—Rewiring: Designing My Next Chapter with Intention After 30 rewarding years in the pharmaceutical industry, I’ve decided not to retire — but to rewire: to reimagine, redesign, and step into a more flexible and intentional new chapter. As I begin this transition, I’m being thoughtful about how I spend my time and energy — focusing on my “Four Fs”: Faith, Family, Friends, and Flexibility. I’m looking forward to creating space for meaningful moments with my granddaughter, giving back in new ways, spending more time in my beloved Dominican Republic, and investing in the people and experiences that matter most. While I’m closing this chapter of full-time leadership, my passion for advancing medicines, supporting innovation, and developing people remains as strong as ever. I look forward to staying engaged in new ways as I explore what this next season may bring. I’m deeply grateful for the lives we’ve touched through medicines and vaccines, for the incredible teams I’ve had the privilege to work with and lead, and for the colleagues, mentors, and advocates who supported me throughout this journey. Most of all, I’m thankful for my family’s unwavering love and support. Here’s to new beginnings, new perspectives, and the freedom to design life with greater intention. #NextChapter #Leadership #Gratitude #LifeDesign #NewBeginnings

Big organizations are rarely simple—but at ViiV, our mission cuts through the complexity. That clarity is what brings us together and drives our decisions as we work to end the HIV epidemic. This week, our US and Global Leadership Teams came together for a focused workshop on across our portfolio —aligning on priorities, innovation, and the work required to deliver meaningful impact for customers and patients in 2026 and beyond. We shared insights, challenged assumptions, and pressure‑tested key decisions to keep strategy, evidence, and execution tightly connected. Thank you to everyone who leaned in with candor, pace, and a bit of laughter—leaving as one team with the conviction and momentum to accelerate what only ViiV exists to do. We won’t stop. #WeWontStop Jean-Bernard Simeon Kimberley Brown Colleen Kamrad Silvia. Guichardo Robert Bowers Jean van Wyk Amanda Mott Bethan Garland Katie Lipscombe Diana Medeiros Plácido
